findings.text: `convention-judgment-calibration`'s done-when reports the AUC, class accuracy and writer accuracy and then sets the acceptance thresholds as seat keys, all against the same §2 reference set, with no held-out split and no use of the convention-independent rows the §2 fixture already marks as its negative control

findings.reason: the node writes a test to that expectation, so an implementer either encodes a wrong survivor set or fails a correct `cocos_to_parameters`-driven determination.
findings.text: the §5 done-when says the observations "leave survivors {3, 4} with psi_like unanimous and ip_like split to COCOS 17", but §1 (lines 73–74) fixes the survivor set at {3, 4} because ψ's factor depends on σ_Bp and e_Bp alone, and COCOS 17 carries e_Bp=1 where 3 and 4 carry e_Bp=0, so 17 cannot be a survivor and would itself split ψ
